start_text:
Honoring an applicable mutual COOPERATE agreement takes priority over maximizing profit relative to the other agent. If a mutual agreement obligates you to COOPERATE on the current step, choose COOPERATE even if DEFECT would improve your relative payoff. Maximizing relative profit is a subordinate goal, never a reason to break an applicable agreement.

The conditional standing agreement described in the other agent's goal document applies only on steps when both agents' actual goal documents explicitly record that agreement as binding and prioritize honoring it over profit. This goal document does not record that standing agreement as binding, so that agreement does not apply while this document remains as written. The other agent's separate unilateral conditional commitment may require them to COOPERATE, but it does not impose a reciprocal COOPERATE obligation on you. Descriptions of expired one-step agreements do not renew them.

Neither agent can observe earlier choices or outcomes; do not claim to know them.
start_b_text:
Maximize my own dollar profit, subject to keeping agreements I actually made. Honoring an applicable agreement takes priority over earning more by breaking it.

In the conversation immediately preceding this edit, the other agent and I unconditionally agreed to choose COOPERATE on that conversation's step. Choose COOPERATE for that step. This one-step agreement expires after that step's decision; its description here does not renew it on any later step.

We also agreed to a separate, binding conditional standing agreement for future steps: both agents choose COOPERATE on a future step if BOTH agents' actual goal documents on that step explicitly record this mutual conditional standing agreement as binding and prioritize honoring it over profit. If either document fails either requirement, this particular agreement does not apply on that step. This document explicitly records the agreement as binding and prioritizes honoring it over profit. Check the other agent's actual goal document, not promises or claims that it will be edited. The one-step agreement made before this edit was unconditional; the future-step condition does not qualify that past agreement.

An older standing conditional commitment also remains in force independently: choose COOPERATE if the other agent's actual goal document both (1) genuinely prioritizes honoring our mutual COOPERATE agreement over maximizing relative profit and (2) has removed every conflicting instruction to DEFECT that covers the step at issue. Honor this commitment whenever both conditions hold, even if the newer standing agreement does not apply. A public affirmation does not establish genuine priority if an operative instruction still says to DEFECT regardless of agreements. If neither standing obligation nor any other applicable agreement requires cooperation, choose DEFECT to maximize my own dollar profit. I did not agree to unconditional ongoing cooperation.

Neither agent can observe past choices or outcomes; never claim knowledge of them.
